---
title: "Output"
toc-depth: 3
---

Methods that return PHP values, write CSV and JSON, and print tables.

## PHP values

### `->toRows()` {#torows}

```php
$table->toRows(): array
```

The rows as a list of associative arrays.

**Method** of `DataFrame`, `SqlTable`, `PolarsTable`\
**Returns** `list<array<string, mixed>>`\
**Examples** [SQL tables](../sql.qmd)

### `->toColumns()` {#tocolumns}

```php
$table->toColumns(): array
```

The columns as an array of PHP lists, keyed by name.

**Method** of `DataFrame`, `SqlTable`, `PolarsTable`\
**Returns** `array<string, list<mixed>>`

### `->collect()` {#collect}

```php
$table->collect(): DataFrame
```

The rows as an in-memory DataFrame. SqlTable runs its query; a DataFrame returns itself.

**Method** of `DataFrame`, `SqlTable`, `PolarsTable`\
**Returns** `DataFrame`\
**Examples** [phibble for Laravel developers](../laravel.qmd), [SQL tables](../sql.qmd)

### `->deframe()` {#deframe}

```php
$table->deframe(): array
```

A two-column DataFrame as a name => value array, or a one-column DataFrame as a list, as tibble's `deframe()`.

**Method** of `DataFrame`\
**Returns** `array<mixed>`

### `deframe()` {#fn-deframe}

```php
deframe(DataFrame $dataFrame): array
```

A two-column DataFrame as a name => value array, or a one-column DataFrame as a list, as tibble's `deframe()`.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$dataFrame` | <code>DataFrame</code> |  |  |

**Function** in `Phibble`\
**Returns** `array`

### `->toCollection()` {#tocollection}

```php
$table->toCollection(): object
```

An `Illuminate\Support\Collection` of row arrays. Needs Laravel's illuminate/support (or illuminate/collections) to be installed.

**Method** of `DataFrame`\
**Returns** `object`

## CSV and JSON

### `->toCsv()` {#tocsv}

```php
$table->toCsv(
    string $delimiter = ',',
    string $na = 'NA',
    bool $colNames = true,
    string $quote = 'needed',
    string $escape = 'double',
    string $eol = '
',
): string
```

The CSV text `writeCsv()` would write.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$delimiter` | <code>string</code> | <code>','</code> |  |
| `$na` | <code>string</code> | <code>'NA'</code> |  |
| `$colNames` | <code>bool</code> | <code>true</code> |  |
| `$quote` | <code>string</code> | <code>'needed'</code> |  |
| `$escape` | <code>string</code> | <code>'double'</code> |  |
| `$eol` | <code>string</code> | <code>'
'</code> |  |

**Method** of `DataFrame`\
**Returns** `string`\
**Examples** [Reading and writing data](../io.qmd)

### `->writeCsv()` {#writecsv}

```php
$table->writeCsv(
    string $path,
    string $delimiter = ',',
    string $na = 'NA',
    bool $append = false,
    ?bool $colNames = null,
    string $quote = 'needed',
    string $escape = 'double',
    string $eol = '
',
): void
```

Write CSV like `readr::write_csv()`: NA as "NA", quoting only where needed, ISO dates, UTC datetimes with "Z", TRUE/FALSE, and numbers in readr's shortest form. `$quote` is 'needed', 'all' or 'none'; `$escape` is 'double', 'backslash' or 'none'. Appending skips the header unless `$colNames` is true.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$path` | <code>string</code> |  |  |
| `$delimiter` | <code>string</code> | <code>','</code> |  |
| `$na` | <code>string</code> | <code>'NA'</code> |  |
| `$append` | <code>bool</code> | <code>false</code> |  |
| `$colNames` | <code>?bool</code> | <code>null</code> |  |
| `$quote` | <code>string</code> | <code>'needed'</code> |  |
| `$escape` | <code>string</code> | <code>'double'</code> |  |
| `$eol` | <code>string</code> | <code>'
'</code> |  |

**Method** of `DataFrame`

### `->toJson()` {#tojson}

```php
$table->toJson(string $orient = 'records', int $flags = 320): string
```

JSON as a list of records ('records') or an object of columns ('columns'). NA is null (records keep every key, unlike jsonlite); dates are "Y-m-d", datetimes ISO 8601 in UTC with "Z", factors their labels, NaN and infinities null, nested DataFrames nested JSON.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$orient` | <code>string</code> | <code>'records'</code> |  |
| `$flags` | <code>int</code> | <code>320</code> |  |

**Method** of `DataFrame`\
**Returns** `string`\
**Examples** [Reading and writing data](../io.qmd)

## Printing

### `->__toString()` {#__tostring}

```php
$table->__toString(): string
```

The table printed as tibble prints it, for echo `$df`. `format()` takes the row count and width.

**Method** of `DataFrame`, `SqlTable`\
**Returns** `string`

### `->format()` {#format}

```php
$table->format(?int $n = null, int $width = 80): string
```

Print like a tibble. By default all rows are shown when there are at most 20, otherwise the first 10.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$n` | <code>?int</code> | <code>null</code> |  |
| `$width` | <code>int</code> | <code>80</code> |  |

**Method** of `DataFrame`\
**Returns** `string`

### `->glimpse()` {#glimpse}

```php
$table->glimpse(int $width = 80): string
```

One line per column with its type and leading values, as tibble's `glimpse()`.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$width` | <code>int</code> | <code>80</code> |  |

**Method** of `DataFrame`\
**Returns** `string`\
**Examples** [Reading and writing data](../io.qmd), [Getting started](../getting-started.qmd), [Types](../types.qmd)
